commit_message:
[ROCDL] Set relaxed buffer OOB mode (#24692)

Recent LLVM changes to ptr addrspace(7)/fat buffer lowering (LLVM PRs
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/134329 and
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/134734 ) mean that
underalligned loads from buffer pointers get devectorized unless
"relaxed mode" is enabled. IREE already has mitigations for the issues
that this OOB mode handles, so we must enable relaxed mode to prevent
severe regressions as seen in #24690.

Sadly there's no test for this one as we don't currently have tests for
the module translation and this is a hotfix so I want to keep it
minimal.

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Add pass to convert broadcast batch_matmul to matmul (#24670)

When a `linalg.batch_matmul` multiplies a batched input by a weight that
is the same for every batch, every batch slice runs the same matmul
against the same weight. This pass rewrites that case into a single
`linalg.matmul`.

For an input of shape `[B, M, K]` and a weight `[K, N]` broadcast to
`[B, K, N]`, the pass:

  1. collapses the input to `[B*M, K]` using tensor.collapse_shape
  2. multiplies it by the `[K, N]` weight using linalg.matmul
  3. expands the result back to `[B, M, N]` using tensor.expand_shape

This removes the broadcast and turns the batched contraction into a
plain
matmul, which downstream passes can handle better.

---------

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU][RISCV] Add RVV bf16 mmt4d ukernel using the Zvfbfwma widening MAC (bf16*bf16->f32)

This commit adds a bf16 x bf16 -> f32 mmt4d microkernel for RISC-V targets
with the `Zvfbfwma` extension, using the `vfwmaccbf16` widening
multiply-accumulate.
Previously a data-tiled bf16 matmul on RISC-V was promoted to f32 and computed
in f32, now it keeps bf16 storage and accumulates into f32 in-register. This is
the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: pre-commit

the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

commit_message:
[ROCDL] Set relaxed buffer OOB mode (#24692)

Recent LLVM changes to ptr addrspace(7)/fat buffer lowering (LLVM PRs
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/134329 and
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/134734 ) mean that
underalligned loads from buffer pointers get devectorized unless
"relaxed mode" is enabled. IREE already has mitigations for the issues
that this OOB mode handles, so we must enable relaxed mode to prevent
severe regressions as seen in #24690.

Sadly there's no test for this one as we don't currently have tests for
the module translation and this is a hotfix so I want to keep it
minimal.
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU][RISCV] Add RVV bf16 mmt4d ukernel using the Zvfbfwma widening MAC (bf16*bf16->f32)

This commit adds a bf16 x bf16 -> f32 mmt4d microkernel for RISC-V targets
with the `Zvfbfwma` extension, using the `vfwmaccbf16` widening
multiply-accumulate.
Previously a data-tiled bf16 matmul on RISC-V was promoted to f32 and computed
in f32, now it keeps bf16 storage and accumulates into f32 in-register. This is
the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: pre-commit

[LLVMCPU][RISCV] Add RVV bf16 mmt4d ukernel using the Zvfbfwma widening MAC (bf16*bf16->f32)

This commit adds a bf16 x bf16 -> f32 mmt4d microkernel for RISC-V targets
with the `Zvfbfwma` extension, using the `vfwmaccbf16` widening
multiply-accumulate.
Previously a data-tiled bf16 matmul on RISC-V was promoted to f32 and computed
in f32, now it keeps bf16 storage and accumulates into f32 in-register. This is
the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_byollvm

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU][RISCV] Add RVV bf16 mmt4d ukernel using the Zvfbfwma widening MAC (bf16*bf16->f32)

This commit adds a bf16 x bf16 -> f32 mmt4d microkernel for RISC-V targets
with the `Zvfbfwma` extension, using the `vfwmaccbf16` widening
multiply-accumulate.
Previously a data-tiled bf16 matmul on RISC-V was promoted to f32 and computed
in f32, now it keeps bf16 storage and accumulates into f32 in-register. This is
the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: Test PJRT plugin / Build and test (ubuntu-24.04, cpu)

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Add pass to convert broadcast batch_matmul to matmul (#24670)

When a `linalg.batch_matmul` multiplies a batched input by a weight that
is the same for every batch, every batch slice runs the same matmul
against the same weight. This pass rewrites that case into a single
`linalg.matmul`.

For an input of shape `[B, M, K]` and a weight `[K, N]` broadcast to
`[B, K, N]`, the pass:

  1. collapses the input to `[B*M, K]` using tensor.collapse_shape
  2. multiplies it by the `[K, N]` weight using linalg.matmul
  3. expands the result back to `[B, M, N]` using tensor.expand_shape

This removes the broadcast and turns the batched contraction into a
plain
matmul, which downstream passes can handle better.

---------

Co-authored-by: ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
feat(tiling): add makeInnerTileAlignmentFn and thread it through tile-and-fuse

Add makeInnerTileAlignmentFn (TileAndFuseUtils), which builds an
InnerTileAlignment control function marking each scalable (dynamic) inner tile
of a tiled/fused linalg.pack/unpack with a given alignment. Thread the control
function through the tile+fuse helpers: fuseProducersOfSlices reads it from
SCFTilingOptions and fuseConsumersIntoForall takes it as an argument. Install it
in LLVMCPUTileAndFuseProducerConsumer with Equal alignment (the vector tile size
equals the scalable inner tile), so scalable linalg.pack/unpack tile and fuse at
the vector level without re-deriving the relationship from scalable IR.

Adds lit coverage in tile_and_fuse_producer_consumer_anchoring_root_op.mlir.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen][RVV]: enable vectorization of scalable mmt4d without masks

This PR makes sure that we can vectorize `(batch_)mmt4d` operations without masks (this is not necesary due to data-tiling having padding semantics).

Additionally, current vectorization path for mmt4d (or other contractions for that matter) vectorizes the operations in the linalg body to a `multi_reduction`, which for `BF16xBF16->FP32` or `INT8xINT8->INT32` has `exti/extf`semantics on the operands. This is not ideal since target ISAs might have specific instructions that could be used for these contractions. If these extensions do not exist, then the extension semantics are inserted by vector lowering passes anyways.

Tests for the assume flags reside upstream, but these tests also showcase this.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[Codegen][RVV]: enable vectorization of scalable mmt4d without masks

This PR makes sure that we can vectorize `(batch_)mmt4d` operations without masks (this is not necesary due to data-tiling having padding semantics).

Additionally, current vectorization path for mmt4d (or other contractions for that matter) vectorizes the operations in the linalg body to a `multi_reduction`, which for `BF16xBF16->FP32` or `INT8xINT8->INT32` has `exti/extf`semantics on the operands. This is not ideal since target ISAs might have specific instructions that could be used for these contractions. If these extensions do not exist, then the extension semantics are inserted by vector lowering passes anyways.

Tests for the assume flags reside upstream, but these tests also showcase this.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Add pass to convert broadcast batch_matmul to matmul (#24670)

When a `linalg.batch_matmul` multiplies a batched input by a weight that
is the same for every batch, every batch slice runs the same matmul
against the same weight. This pass rewrites that case into a single
`linalg.matmul`.

For an input of shape `[B, M, K]` and a weight `[K, N]` broadcast to
`[B, K, N]`, the pass:

  1. collapses the input to `[B*M, K]` using tensor.collapse_shape
  2. multiplies it by the `[K, N]` weight using linalg.matmul
  3. expands the result back to `[B, M, N]` using tensor.expand_shape

This removes the broadcast and turns the batched contraction into a
plain
matmul, which downstream passes can handle better.

  2. multiplies it by the `[K, N]` weight using linalg.matmul
  3. expands the result back to `[B, M, N]` using tensor.expand_shape

This removes the broadcast and turns the batched contraction into a
plain
matmul, which downstream passes can handle better.

commit_message:
[ROCDL] Set relaxed buffer OOB mode (#24692)

Recent LLVM changes to ptr addrspace(7)/fat buffer lowering (LLVM PRs
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/134329 and
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/134734 ) mean that
underalligned loads from buffer pointers get devectorized unless
"relaxed mode" is enabled. IREE already has mitigations for the issues
that this OOB mode handles, so we must enable relaxed mode to prevent
severe regressions as seen in #24690.

Sadly there's no test for this one as we don't currently have tests for
the module translation and this is a hotfix so I want to keep it
minimal.
name: macos_x64_clang

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU][RISCV] Add RVV bf16 mmt4d ukernel using the Zvfbfwma widening MAC (bf16*bf16->f32)

This commit adds a bf16 x bf16 -> f32 mmt4d microkernel for RISC-V targets
with the `Zvfbfwma` extension, using the `vfwmaccbf16` widening
multiply-accumulate.
Previously a data-tiled bf16 matmul on RISC-V was promoted to f32 and computed
in f32, now it keeps bf16 storage and accumulates into f32 in-register. This is
the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: runtime :: windows-2022

[LLVMCPU][RISCV] Add RVV bf16 mmt4d ukernel using the Zvfbfwma widening MAC (bf16*bf16->f32)

This commit adds a bf16 x bf16 -> f32 mmt4d microkernel for RISC-V targets
with the `Zvfbfwma` extension, using the `vfwmaccbf16` widening
multiply-accumulate.
Previously a data-tiled bf16 matmul on RISC-V was promoted to f32 and computed
in f32, now it keeps bf16 storage and accumulates into f32 in-register. This is
the bf16 analog of the int8 kernel from #23734. When implementing, i was also
looking at the f16 Zvfh path from #22231 a lot.

Summary of changes:
- a new `zvfbfwma` RISC-V CPU feature bit
- CPU encoding tile enumeration for RVV bf16->f32 matmul (enabled by `+zvfbfwma`)
- a new RVV intrinsic-based bf16 mmt4d ukernel (mmt4d_riscv_64_zvfbfwma.c)
  along with tile registration, entry-point selection, and CMake/Bazel builds
- mmt4d_test coverage for bf16*bf16->f32

bf16 without Zvfbfwma still promotes to f32.

How this change was tested: I compiled with iree-compile for `rv64gcv+zvfbfwma`
and confirmed the dispatch data-tiles to mmt4d with vfwmaccbf16 in the
generated code (no f32 promotion). Numerics and tile selection were checked
using qemu-riscv64 (all M0 tiles, accumulate on/off) against an f32 reference.

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: Test RISC-V 64 / riscv64

commit_message:
[Codegen][RVV]: enable vectorization of scalable mmt4d without masks

This PR makes sure that we can vectorize `(batch_)mmt4d` operations without masks (this is not necesary due to data-tiling having padding semantics).

Additionally, current vectorization path for mmt4d (or other contractions for that matter) vectorizes the operations in the linalg body to a `multi_reduction`, which for `BF16xBF16->FP32` or `INT8xINT8->INT32` has `exti/extf`semantics on the operands. This is not ideal since target ISAs might have specific instructions that could be used for these contractions. If these extensions do not exist, then the extension semantics are inserted by vector lowering passes anyways.

Tests for the assume flags reside upstream, but these tests also showcase this.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: Test AMD MI355 / test_mi355
